front_question: Define a Tangent to a circle and its Point of Contact.
back_answer: A tangent to a circle is a straight line that intersects (touches) the circle at exactly one point. The point where the tangent touches the circle is called the point of contact.

front_question: State Theorem 10.1 regarding radius and tangent at the point of contact.
back_answer: The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact. (OP ⊥ XY at P).

front_question: State Theorem 10.2 regarding tangents drawn from an external point.
back_answer: The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal. (PQ = PR from point P).

front_question: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle: (i) from a point inside, (ii) on the circle, (iii) from an external point?
back_answer:
(i) Inside: 0 tangents.
(ii) On the circle: exactly 1 tangent.
(iii) External point: exactly 2 tangents.

front_question: Prove that the tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter of a circle are parallel.
back_answer: Let AB be a diameter. Tangents at A and B are perpendicular to AB (Theorem 10.1). Thus the interior angles on the same side of transversal AB sum to 90° + 90° = 180° (or alternate interior angles are equal to 90°), proving the tangents are parallel.
